scams.name: Tulum Ruins 'Conservation Fee' & Mandatory Guide Scam
scams.description: Tulum Archaeological Zone is Mexico's most-visited Caribbean-coast Mayan ruins — and hosts a 2025 'conservation fee' + 'mandatory guide' scam ecosystem. Multiple 2025 traveler reports document this pattern, including first-person accounts of the 'Tulum Tax Scam,' the cross-site 'Conservation Fee Scam' in Cancún, 2025 fee controversy covering Tulum and Akumal, and adjacent warnings about Chichen Itzá tour scams. Legitimate costs: Tulum ruins entry is MX$100 (INAH federal). NO additional 'conservation fee' exists. Optional licensed guides charge MX$800–$1,200 PER GROUP (4–8 people), not per person. Parking at OFFICIAL lot is MX$150. The 2025 scams: (a) 'ecological conservation fee MX$500 per person' demanded at gate by touts in uniforms — fake; (b) 'mandatory Mayan guide MX$600 per person' at entrance — NO guide required; self-guided maps free; (c) ticket-seller imposters 200m before gate selling 'combined ticket MX$800' — no combo exists; (d) 'parking fee MX$500' at unofficial lots (real MX$150); (e) 'cenote + ruins combo MX$2,000 per person' bundled with commission-stop lunch; (f) 'photo package MX$400' upsell at the Castillo viewpoint; (g) 'mandatory donation to Mayan community MX$200' post-visit. For older travelers: (1) buy Tulum ruins entry at the OFFICIAL INAH ticket window — MX$100 per foreigner; no additional fees; (2) park ONLY at the OFFICIAL lot MX$150 with government-issued receipt; ignore 'unofficial' touts directing elsewhere; (3) NO mandatory guide — self-guide with free INAH map; optional licensed guides are MX$800–$1,200 PER GROUP (verify license badge with photo + number); (4) REFUSE every 'conservation fee', 'Mayan community donation', 'photo package' demand; (5) arrive at 8 AM opening — by 10 AM tour buses flood the site; (6) wear comfortable walking shoes, hat, sun protection; the site is exposed and hot 35°C+ summer; (7) for swimming at the adjacent beach, walk down from the ruins — beach access is MX$50 if via the site; (8) traveler reports have specific tout-location warnings to memorise.
scams.avoidance: Pay ONLY MX$100 at official INAH ticket window; no extra fees Park at OFFICIAL lot MX$150 with government receipt NO mandatory guide; optional MX$800–$1,200 PER GROUP REFUSE every 'conservation fee', 'donation', 'photo package' demand Arrive 8 AM opening before tour-bus flood
scams.location: Tulum Archaeological Zone entrance (Zona Arqueológica de Tulum), parking-lot approach, 'Mayan guide' tout zone at gate, ticket-seller imposters

scams.name: Tulum Beach Zone 'Hotel Zone' Restaurant Bill-Padding & Beach Club Upcharge
scams.description: Tulum's 'Zona Hotelera' (Beach Zone, 6 km south of Downtown Tulum) hosts Mexico's most-infamous 2025 restaurant-bill padding ecosystem. Traveler reports document the pattern, including first-person 2025 accounts and the surcharge controversy covering Tulum and Akumal. The 2025 scams: (a) Beach Road restaurants with USD-only menus at 2–3x Mexico norms (US$18 for breakfast, US$35+ for mains); (b) 'service charge 18%' pre-added + tip line (double-tipping trap); (c) credit-card surcharge 10–18% added unannounced; (d) 'environmental fee MX$150 per person' surcharge at some beach restaurants (fake); (e) Beach Club 'entry minimum US$50 per person food/drink' + 'VIP bed US$200' that's an uncovered wooden platform; (f) 'bottle minimum US$300+' at trendy beach clubs (Papaya Playa, Nomade) — one bottle of mid-shelf tequila US$400; (g) 'photo package US$100' upsells from Beach Road nightclubs; (h) 'cash only' smaller restaurants with 'no receipt' policy (chargeback-proof); (i) bill switcheroo where itemised receipt ≠ card charge. For older travelers: (1) eat in DOWNTOWN TULUM (not Beach Zone) — restaurants on Av. Tulum and Av. Satélite have authentic Yucatec food at 1/3 Beach Zone prices; reputable: Charly's Vegan Tacos, Antojitos La Chiapaneca, El Tacoqueto; (2) if you DO go to Beach Zone, budget US$60–$100 per person for a meal regardless of 'deals'; (3) INSPECT the bill line-by-line; refuse 'environmental fee', 'service charge + tip' double-dipping, and 10–18% card surcharges; (4) for Beach Clubs, confirm the MINIMUM + any 'VIP' charge BEFORE sitting; photograph the menu; (5) REFUSE 'bottle minimum' — order drinks individually off the menu; (6) USD menus usually pad the exchange by 10–15% — ask for MX$ bill; (7) traveler reports note the region has higher legitimate VAT (IVA 16%) but it should be in menu prices not added on; (8) bring a calculator and verify totals; (9) pay with credit card (chargeback leverage) not cash where possible.
scams.avoidance: Eat in DOWNTOWN TULUM (Av. Tulum/Satélite): 1/3 Beach Zone prices Reputable: Charly's Vegan Tacos, Antojitos La Chiapaneca, El Tacoqueto Inspect bill; refuse 'service + tip' double; card surcharge 0–3% Beach Club: confirm minimum + VIP charge BEFORE sitting Request MX$ bill (not USD which pads 10–15% exchange)
scams.location: Tulum Beach Road (Carretera Tulum-Boca Paila), Papaya Playa Project, Nomade, Be Tulum, Azulik, La Zebra beach-restaurant cluster

scams.name: Tulum Cenote Tour Unlicensed Operator & Fake 'Private Access'
scams.description: Tulum is surrounded by world-class cenotes (Dos Ojos, Gran Cenote, Cenote Calavera, Casa Cenote) and the tour ecosystem hosts a 2025 unlicensed-operator + entry-fee overcharge pattern. Multiple 2025 community discussions cover cenote tour scams, cross-region cenote guidance, and documented 2025 traveler experiences. Legitimate costs: Gran Cenote entry MX$500, Cenote Dos Ojos MX$350, Cenote Calavera MX$250, Cenote Cristal MX$250, Casa Cenote MX$150. Reputable small-group tour (3–4 cenotes + transport + lunch) MX$1,500–$2,500 per person. The 2025 scams: (a) Downtown Tulum tour booths selling 'private cenote access MX$3,500 per person' when public entry is MX$250–$500; (b) 'VIP guide + underwater photo package' bundle MX$5,000 (photos rarely delivered); (c) fake 'mandatory Mayan shaman cleansing MX$800' at cenote entry; (d) unlicensed tour operators without life jackets, insurance, or SEMARNAT permits; (e) 'exclusive Dos Ojos underwater cave dive MX$8,000' for non-certified visitors (cave diving requires full cave certification — this is either fraud or dangerous); (f) 'commission restaurant' added to tour route; (g) 'life-jacket rental MX$200' at cenotes where jackets are INCLUDED in entry; (h) rental-car drivers directed to 'better cenote' by hotel concierge (commission shop). For older travelers: (1) drive yourself (rental car or Uber day-hire) to cenote entries — Dos Ojos MX$350, Gran Cenote MX$500, Cenote Calavera MX$250 — pay official ticket window; (2) book guided tours ONLY via Google 4.7+ operators: Jugo Cenote Experiences, Mex-On Adventures, Yuchitur — MX$1,500–$2,500 per person for 3-cenote day; (3) REFUSE every 'private cenote access', 'Mayan shaman', 'VIP guide package' upsell; (4) for Dos Ojos, accept ONLY open-water snorkel (not cave dive unless fully cave-certified with your own instructor); (5) bring biodegradable sunscreen ONLY (chemical sunscreens damage cenote ecosystems — some sites require rinse-off); (6) older-traveler-friendly cenotes: Casa Cenote (easy shore entry), Cenote Cristal (walkway + platform); (7) avoid Gran Cenote 11 AM–3 PM (tour-bus flood); (8) 2–3 cenotes in one day is enough; 4+ is exhausting for older travelers.
scams.avoidance: Pay at official cenote windows: Dos Ojos MX$350, Gran MX$500 Tours via Jugo Cenote, Mex-On, Yuchitur (Google 4.7+) REFUSE 'private access', 'shaman', 'VIP package' upsells NO cave dive unless fully cave-certified with own instructor Biodegradable sunscreen only; 2–3 cenotes max per day
scams.location: Gran Cenote, Cenote Dos Ojos, Cenote Calavera, Cenote Cristal, hotel-lobby tour desks, Downtown Tulum Av. Tulum tour-booking strip

scams.name: Tulum 'Eco-Luxury' Hotel Zone Airbnb & Booking Fraud
scams.description: Tulum's rapid 'eco-luxury' boom 2020–2025 has outpaced legitimate accommodation supply, creating a 2025 fake-listing + price-gouging ecosystem. Traveler reports document 2025 patterns and establish baselines. The 2025 scams: (a) fake Airbnb 'eco-luxury jungle cabaña' listings using stolen photos — properties don't exist or are 200m inland (not 'beachfront'); (b) Instagram DM/WhatsApp 'exclusive private villa rental' at US$400/night requiring full upfront payment via bank transfer; (c) Facebook 'Tulum Luxury Villas' groups with fake profiles — pattern identical to Seminyak Bali villa scams; (d) confirmed-booking cancellations during high season (Dec–Mar, July–Aug) with re-listing at 3–5x rate; (e) on-arrival bait-and-switch to inferior properties; (f) 'cleaning deposit US$150' cash that never returns; (g) 'no-electricity, bio-toilet only' surprises pitched as 'eco-authentic' when really just power failures; (h) 'mandatory gratuity 15–20%' added at beach-road 'managed' cabañas that's pocketed by middlemen. For older travelers: (1) book Tulum accommodations ONLY via Booking.com, Hotels.com, Expedia (platform-protected); OR direct from verified hotel websites (Be Tulum, Papaya Playa Project, Nomade, La Zebra) — all with Booking.com 4.7+ ratings; (2) AVOID Instagram DM, WhatsApp-only, Facebook group, and small-time 'villa manager' listings; (3) NEVER bank-transfer to private sellers — platform secure payment only; (4) for peak season (Dec–Mar, July–Aug), book 4–6 months ahead on Booking.com with free cancellation; (5) AVOID Airbnb for peak season on Tulum — cancellation pattern is documented; (6) confirm BEACH access in writing ('beachfront' vs '2-minute walk to beach' are very different) — some eco-cabañas are actually 200–500m inland; (7) confirm POWER, AC, WIFI status in writing — some 'eco' properties have only generator power 3 hours/night; (8) for older travelers, prefer actual hotels over 'cabaña' concepts; (9) budget: Tulum Beach Zone is US$300–$1,500+ per night peak season; Downtown Tulum is US$60–$200 for far better value.
scams.avoidance: Book ONLY via Booking.com, Hotels.com, Expedia (platform protection) AVOID Instagram DM, WhatsApp, Facebook group listings NEVER bank-transfer to private sellers Confirm BEACH, POWER, AC, WIFI status in writing Prefer Downtown Tulum US$60–$200 vs Beach Zone US$300+
scams.location: Tulum Beach Road hotel-zone Airbnb listings, 'eco-luxury cabaña' social-media promotions, Facebook Tulum Villas groups, Instagram-DM 'jungle casita' offers

scams.name: Tulum Beach Zone Rental-Car Theft & 'Broken Meter' Parking Shakedown
scams.description: Tulum Beach Road has a documented 2025 parking-enforcement + rental-car break-in ecosystem that mirrors the Playa del Carmen highway-checkpoint pattern. Traveler reports document the 'Police scam' pattern with first-person 2025 accounts and broader community baselines. The 2025 scams: (a) 'parking enforcement officer' (fake or real municipal) at Beach Road 'finding' infractions — MX$1,500–$5,000 cash demanded; (b) 'boot removal fee' at parking-restricted zones where your car has been 'booted' for 'wrong parking' — MX$2,000; (c) rental-car window smash-and-grab at unguarded beach parking (Sian Ka'an approach, Ruins Beach) while tourist is in the water; (d) 'parking attendant' demanding Rp 500–1,000 cash deposit with 'we watch your car' — then doesn't actually watch; (e) rental-car GPS-tracker theft where unattended car is stolen from Beach Road; (f) 'car damage during parking' fraud at return (same pattern as Isla/Holbox golf cart); (g) 'broken meter fee' ticket on windshield demanding MX$500 cash to pay at 'nearby' kiosk (fraud). For older travelers: (1) use Uber or taxi for Beach Zone visits — avoid rental car if possible; Tulum Beach Road has limited legitimate parking, and unattended rental cars are theft targets; (2) if driving, park ONLY at hotel valet (free for hotel guests) OR at pay-to-park lots with receipt; (3) NEVER leave anything visible in rental car — bags, phones, cameras must be in trunk or with you; (4) if 'parking enforcement' approaches, ask for BADGE + officer number and written ticket (NOT cash); (5) REFUSE 'boot removal fee' and 'broken meter' windshield tickets demanding cash — legitimate tickets are PAID at the treasury office with written stub; (6) for Sian Ka'an (1-hour drive), park at designated Muyil entry point with ranger station — not informal roadside pullouts; (7) rental-car theft requires police denuncia at Ministerio Público Tulum (+52 984 871 2109) within 24 hours for insurance claim; (8) bring sufficient rental insurance — Mexican third-party liability + comprehensive; (9) traveler reports have specific location warnings.
scams.avoidance: Use Uber/taxi for Beach Zone; avoid rental-car parking If driving, hotel valet OR pay-to-park lot with receipt only NEVER leave anything visible in rental car REFUSE 'boot fee' and 'broken meter' windshield-ticket cash demands Tulum MP (+52 984 871 2109) for theft denuncia within 24 hours
scams.location: Tulum Beach Road parking, hotel-zone parking enforcement checkpoints, Ruins Beach parking, Sian Ka'an approach road

scams.name: Tulum Airport (TQO) 'Mandatory Tourism Tax' & Ticket Verification Scam
scams.description: Tulum opened a new international airport (TQO) in December 2023 and hosts a 2025 departure-scam ecosystem mirroring Cancún's Visitax fraud. Traveler reports document the 'Tulum Tax Scam,' the cross-site 'Conservation Fee Scam' in Cancún, and 2025 posts bluntly titled 'DON'T PAY BULLSHIT EXIT-TAX!' covering the regional fraud. The 2025 scams: (a) 'Visitax verification agent' at TQO departure demanding US$30–$60 per person 'before you can board' — real Visitax is MX$271 paid ONLINE via visitax.gob.mx; (b) 'tourism tax processing fee' tablet-based phishing that clones credit cards; (c) 'luggage inspection fee' Rp 200–500 per bag demanded unofficially; (d) 'mandatory passport re-stamping fee US$15' — no such fee; (e) WhatsApp phishing texts claiming 'your Tulum departure tax is unpaid'; (f) 'skip the line US$25' upsell at immigration (no skip-line exists); (g) fake 'FMM return form fee' — the tourist-card return is free. For older travelers: (1) pay Visitax ONLY via visitax.gob.mx (official Quintana Roo government portal) BEFORE your trip — save PDF confirmation to phone; MX$271 per person ages 4+; (2) IGNORE every TQO 'tax agent' or 'processing fee' approach — the government does NOT collect tax at the airport; (3) the ONLY legitimate airport fees are ticket-price-inclusive airport taxes (shown on your boarding pass) and Visitax (paid online pre-trip); (4) NEVER hand your credit card at any airport 'tax payment' kiosk or tablet; (5) REFUSE every 'luggage inspection', 'passport re-stamping', 'FMM fee' demand — none is legitimate; (6) if pressured, show your visitax.gob.mx PDF and walk to the airline counter; (7) WhatsApp/SMS 'unpaid tax' texts are phishing — ignore, don't click links; (8) traveler reports have specific TQO-airport warnings; (9) US Embassy 24-hr +52 55 8526 2561 if escalated.
scams.avoidance: Pay Visitax ONLY via visitax.gob.mx BEFORE trip (MX$271 pp) Save PDF confirmation; show if challenged IGNORE every TQO airport 'tax agent' approach NEVER hand card at any airport 'tax' kiosk or tablet Refuse 'luggage/passport/FMM' fee demands — none exist
scams.location: Tulum Felipe Carrillo Puerto Airport (TQO) departures, 'Visitax verification' kiosks, 'tourism tax processing' booths, immigration-approach touts
